newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PMs issue orders in bid to halt clashes.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PMs issue orders in bid to halt clashes.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen on Wednesday issued orders aimed at averting further armed clashes between their rival parties.

The premiers, who formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993, signed directives to stop the unauthorised movement of armed forces, the illegal recruitment of military forces and the unauthorised possession of arms.

They signed the orders in their capacities as joint supreme commanders of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces (RCAF) after a meeting on Wednesday morning of top military officials, co-Defence Minister Tea Banh said.
A copy of the directive seen by Reuters said the orders were being made "to protect the safety for the people and public order security".

Friction between forces of Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party and the Cambodian People's Party of Hun Sen flamed into fighting earlier this month which left a number of people dead over several days in Battambang province.
CPP's Tea Banh and his co-Defence Minister Tea Chamrath from FUNCINPEC were sent to Battambang on February 14 to calm tensions and order their respective troops to pull back.
A few days later Ranariddh and Hun Sen agreed to recall four feuding officials blamed for the clashes.
